title: Gate record
description: What one gate run decided and why: the audit record `aidd gate --record` writes (`aidd-record.json` in CI, kept as a workflow artifact). Each field says what it evidences, so an auditor can sample records against a control. A record is a fact about the run that produced it; the commit status posted by the gate App and the CI run log are the tamper-evident anchors for it. `aidd gate --json` prints the same record, with `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: `aidd gate --json` only: the version of the printed record, as for the other --json outputs. The file `--record` writes leaves it out; its `aidd_version` says which release wrote it.

aidd_version.description: The aidd release whose gate judged the change, so the rules that applied are known.

decision.description: The verdict the gate posted: pass may merge, pending waits, fail blocks.

failed_rules.description: Rules at fail level; `aidd gate --explain <rule>` states each one.

pending_rules.description: Rules still waiting on a human or on evidence.

findings.description: Every finding, with the stable code that says which check fired. Messages are for people; codes are what tools and the conformance suite compare.

rule.description: The gate rule that found it.

code.description: The stable finding code, such as `scope.outside` (the rulebook lists them).

change.description: The PR/MR number or local ref under review.

head_sha.description: The exact commit judged. Evidence, approvals, and the posted status bind to it.

base_sha.description: The base commit the diff and the red run were measured against.

platform.description: github, gitlab, local, or another adapter.

trusted.description: Whether the platform supplied the facts (CI) or a local, untrusted context built them. A local record is never evidence.

config_sha256.description: Digest of the base-branch config with its org preset and parents: the policy in force when the change was judged.

config_mode.description: The mode the base branch's resolved config sets, when it sets one. It wins over the CI setting.

profile.description: The conformance profile that set the gate strictness.

tenant.description: The tenant the repository's config names (`tenant`), or null: whose Approvers this decision counted.

spec.description: The Spec path, or null for an inline change.

spec_approved_by.description: The Approvers of that exact hash.

spec_approval_before_implementation.description: Whether its approval named a commit that held only the Spec, its frozen files, and the goal's other work.

specs.description: A goal's change (the Change Request block's `specs`): each Spec it carries, as the gate judged it. `spec` and `spec_id` are null then.

spec_id.description: The Spec's id, or null for an inline change.

trace_id.description: The id that links this change to its Spec, its ticket, and sibling changes in other repositories: traceability.

owner_team.description: The team accountable for the Spec, from its `owner_team`.

route.description: The route applied, after the gate's own assessment.

declared_route.description: Present only when the gate raised the declared route (a normal Spec raised to major).

required_route.description: The minimum route the real diff requires; routes only go up.

route_reasons.description: Why that minimum: the rules and paths that raised it (impact analysis).

required_pools.description: The specialist Approver pools the change needs.

type.description: The kind of change, in Conventional Commits vocabulary.

confidence.description: The confidence the assessment declared; low stops the run.

risk.description: The declared blast radius and risk dimensions.

residual_risk.description: The risk that remains after the rollback plan, as declared.

scope.description: The paths the change was allowed to touch.

scope_declared.description: Whether the scope was declared or taken from the changed paths (minor changes).

declaration.description: Where the change's declaration came from: `block`, a Change Request block; `derived`, none, so the gate took it from facts it checks: a bot's standard change class, the one Spec the diff carries, or else the route computed from the diff, the type from the commit subjects, and `assisted_by` from the commit trailers.

revert_of.description: An emergency that is an exact revert of this commit, merged on the base: it landed on the commander's approval alone.

phase.description: A Spec-backed change's phase: spec while every changed path is the Spec, its frozen test and design files, or its backfill, and a Task has yet to change anything (the gate waits for Spec approval, and failing tests are expected); implementation after.

plan.description: Plan adherence for a Spec: how many Tasks it planned, and which changed nothing in their scope.

tasks.description: How many Tasks the Spec planned.

untouched_tasks.description: The ids of the Tasks that changed nothing in their scope.

changed_paths.description: Every path the change touched, as the platform reported it.

changed_lines.description: Lines changed, as the changed-line limit counts them, excluding changed_lines_exclude_paths and the Spec's frozen files.

binary_files.description: The number of binary files in the change; a binary file rules out the minor route.

authors.description: Everyone accountable for the change: the PR/MR author, every commit author and committer. No one in this list may approve it.

separation_of_duties.description: Whether approvals had to come from outside the authors, or the solo profile waived it and recorded the waiver.

spec_hash.description: The 128-bit hash of the Spec, its test files, and its design files, as approved at Spec approval.

spec_approved_by.description: The Approvers of that exact hash: Spec approval, the authorization of what will be built.

spec_approval_before_implementation.description: Whether an approval named a commit holding only the Spec and its frozen files, proving Spec approval came before the code.

approved_by.description: The Approvers of the head commit: Merge approval, the authorization of what was built.

spec_approvals.description: Each counted Spec approval: who, when the approval comment was posted, and the commit it named (null when it named none).

merge_approvals.description: Each counted Merge approval: who, when, and the head commit it binds to.

evidence_runner.description: The CI run that produced the test evidence, as the evidence file names it (`ci`, `run_id`, `url`).

specialist_approved_by.description: Per required pool, the specialist Approvers who approved the head.

policy.description: The result of the organization's Policy command for this change.

status_checks.description: Existing CI check runs reused as evidence, with the state each had on the head.

tests.description: Each required test command's result on the head: an exit code from a defined runner, never a claim.

source.description: Where the command was declared: the config or the Spec.

command.description: The command, as an argument list.

exit.description: The exit code on the head commit, or null when it did not run.

duration_seconds.description: How long it ran, in seconds; null when unknown.

red_exit.description: The exit code of the same command on the base commit, when it ran there (red-then-green).

red_status.description: The status of the run on the base commit.

flaky.description: True when it passed on head only after a retry: counted green, and counted flaky by metrics.

shared_with.description: Set when the head is shared with another pull request into a protected base and the worse decision was posted.

merge_queue_sha.description: Set when the decision is for a merge queue entry: the entry's commit whose tests ran and on which the status is posted. `head_sha` stays the pull request head the approvals bind to.
